newsitem.title: FRANCE: French stocks open higher, Gen des Eaux rallies.
newsitem.headline: French stocks open higher, Gen des Eaux rallies.

text.p: French stocks opened higher on Friday, buoyed by Wall Street's gains and the U.S. Federal Reserve's decision to let interest rates stand, brokers said.
The blue-chip CAC-40 index was up 10.62 points, or 0.42 percent, at 2,569.05 at 0910 GMT after hitting an all-time high of 2,570.49. The CAC-40 February futures contract was up 11 points at 2,576.
Volume in the first 30 minutes was 1.4 billion francs.
After two consecutive record closes on Wednesday and Thursday, the CAC index has risen above the objectives set by most market experts.
A few analysts view the market as oversold, but others remain bullish, citing favourable currency and interest rate trends and the benefits of recent corporate restructurings.
Jacques Chahine of consultants Jacques Chahine Finance said he expects the CAC to rise to 2,700 within six months. "This rise can't last forever but I think it'll go on for a while," he said.
Some investors were cautious ahead of the release, due at 1330 GMT, of the market-moving U.S. unemployment figures for January.
Shares in Generale des Eaux, suspending on Thursday pending an announcement of a restructuring of its media activities with media group Havas, rallied 5.18 percent to 773 francs.

The companies said Generale des Eaux would become the majority shareholder of Havas with 30 percent, and Havas would become the leading shareholder in Canal Plus with 34.4 percent as part of the restructuring.

CGE said it would sell Havas its 19.3 percent stake in pay-television company Canal Plus for 5.6 billion francs and its Generale d'Images unit for 526 million. It will obtain a stake of some 30 percent in Havas through the issue of new shares in exchange for the assets and the purchase of eight million Havas shares for 3.4 billion francs from Alcatel Alsthom.
"It's a very good deal for Generale des Eaux," a trader said. "As for Havas...some sellers may regret it because we may be in for good surprises from them in terms of asset sales."

Shares in Elf-Aquitaine snapped a recent rally to fall 1.2 percent to 577 francs. Financial group Paribas said it sold the remainder of its stake in Elf, or around two million shares, in New York. Some market sources said they were priced at 555 francs and others at 557 francs each.
Paribas' stock was 0.94 percent higher at 397.60 francs.

Shares in hotel group Accor, which fell 1.2 percent on Thursday, dropped a 1.08 percent at 732 francs. Fund managers said Societe Generale de Belgique was preparing to sell its holding in Accor. Its stake was nine percent last June.

Shares in luxury goods group LVMH were down 0.99 percent at 1,406 francs. The Wall Street Journal said it was in advanced talks to buy out the remainder of U.S. duty free chain DFS from the last dissident shareholder Robert Miller. It said a deal could be struck in a matter of weeks.
No one at LVMH was immediately available for comment.
